subject: MAT
label: Grade 10
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 10 Mathematics, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 11 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Real numbers
modules.outcome: apply Euclid's division lemma and fundamental theorem of arithmetic
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Real numbers', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: apply Euclid's division lemma and fundamental theorem of arithmetic. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Show it with objects or a picture: build or draw the idea in 'Real numbers' before using symbols.
Say the rule in your own words, then write one worked line, naming each step.
Use it: apply Euclid's division lemma and fundamental theorem of arithmetic. Start with one easy question, then one with a real-life story.
Check it: use a second method, estimate, or work backwards to test your answer.
modules.example: Solved: Square root of 196: 14 x 14 = 196, so the root is 14. 2 cubed x 2 to the 4 = 2 to the 7 = 128. 0.75 = 3/4 is rational; the square root of 2 is not. Method: Model run for 'Real numbers'. Read the question and underline what is asked. Draw or write what is known. Choose the method named in the unit. Work it line by line, one idea per line, with units where they apply. Estimate first so the answer can be tested for sense. Check by working backwards. What a good answer looks like: correct method, every step visible, units stated, and a one-line check.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Apply Euclid's division lemma and fundamental theorem of arithmetic: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Real numbers), and at which Bloom level is it?
'apply', at the Apply level.
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 11 (Statistics and probability) run?
Weeks 35 to 36.
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: count, add and subtract small numbers; name shapes.
L2: use the four operations, fractions and simple measures.
L3: work with ratio, algebra beginnings and geometry reasoning.
L4: algebra, geometry proof, trigonometry and statistics.
L5: functions, calculus, vectors and probability.
L6 (degree): proof, linear algebra and modelling.
L7 (postgraduate): research mathematics, data science or teaching at depth.
